# Sprout

> Sprout is a free iPhone app that counts your squats with the camera. Every squat grows a plant, and every day you train becomes a plant in your garden.

## Facts

- What it is: an iPhone app that counts bodyweight squats with the camera and grows a plant from them. Each day of training becomes a plant in a garden.
- Platform: iPhone, iOS 17 or later. An Android version is in development.
- Price: free. No subscription and no ads. The only thing sold is "dew", an in-app currency that is also earned by doing squats.
- Counting: the camera picture is analysed on the phone (Apple body-pose detection). No video or photo is recorded, saved or sent.
- Daily goal: 50 squats by default, adjustable. The first five squats of the day water a seed; the plant flowers when the goal is reached.
- Water levels: twelve, from Rain to Sunwater. Lifetime squats raise the level, and a higher level makes each squat grow the plant further.
- Friends: free. Friends can visit each other's gardens and leave a butterfly with a short note. People can be blocked and reported.
- App languages (21): English, Norwegian, Swedish, Danish, Finnish, German, Dutch, French, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, Polish, Turkish, Russian, Hindi, Indonesian, Vietnamese, Thai, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean.
- Name: Sprout in English. In every other language the app carries that language's word for a sprout: Spire (Norsk), Keimling (Deutsch), Pousse (Français), Brote (Español), Broto (Português), 新芽 (日本語), 새싹 (한국어), Grodd (Svenska), Spire (Dansk), Verso (Suomi), Spruit (Nederlands), Germoglio (Italiano), Kiełek (Polski), Filiz (Türkçe), Росток (Русский), अंकुर (हिन्दी), Tunas (Bahasa Indonesia), Mầm (Tiếng Việt), ต้นอ่อน (ไทย), 幼芽 (繁體中文).
- Status (15 November 2026): not yet on the App Store; the version with 21 languages is being prepared for Apple's review.
- Publisher: Esbjug Consult. Contact: sproutappsupport@proton.me

## Pages in English

- [Sprout](https://esbjugconsult.com/sprout/en/): the app shown live, chapter by chapter

## Articles (English), each with its sources

- [Are squats at home good for you?](https://esbjugconsult.com/sprout/en/articles/squats-at-home): Bodyweight squats at home count as muscle-strengthening exercise. What the WHO recommends, what the research shows about strength training and health, and where the evidence stops.
- [How many squats a day should you do?](https://esbjugconsult.com/sprout/en/articles/how-many-squats-a-day): There is no official number of squats per day. A practical answer based on the WHO guidelines and the research on strength training: where to start, how to build up, and when more stops helping.
- [How to do a squat correctly at home](https://esbjugconsult.com/sprout/en/articles/how-to-squat): Step-by-step bodyweight squat technique for home: stance, depth, knees and back, the most common mistakes, and what the research says about deep squats and the knees.
- [What muscles do squats work?](https://esbjugconsult.com/sprout/en/articles/muscles-squats-work): Squats mainly work the quadriceps and the gluteus maximus, with the hamstrings, calves and trunk muscles helping. What each muscle does in a squat, how depth and stance change the work, and what squats leave out.
- [A 30-day squat plan for beginners](https://esbjugconsult.com/sprout/en/articles/30-day-squat-plan): A simple 30-day bodyweight squat plan for beginners: start with 10 squats a day and reach 50 a day in a month, in one to five minutes daily. With the reasoning behind each step.
- [Squats at your desk: breaking up a day of sitting](https://esbjugconsult.com/sprout/en/articles/squats-at-your-desk): If you sit most of the day, a few squats every half hour is a small, studied way to break it up. What the WHO says about sitting, what a University of Toronto trial found, and how to do it at work.
- [How to make squats a daily habit](https://esbjugconsult.com/sprout/en/articles/daily-squat-habit): What the research says about forming an exercise habit: it takes about two months on average, missing one day does not matter, and small and specific beats ambitious. Practical steps for a daily squat habit.
